newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Second night of army rampages in Zaire town.
newsitem.headline: Second night of army rampages in Zaire town.

text.p: Drunk and ill-disciplined soldiers who drifted west after their defeat by Tutsi rebels in east Zaire subjected the town of Kisangani to a second night of shooting and looting, witnesses said on Sunday.
One unconfirmed report said one soldier had been shot dead by troops seeking to restore order. There were no other immediate reports of casualties.

Kisangani, about 500 km (325 miles) from the conflict zone, is a likely staging post for any relief operation for Hutu refugees who are believed to have trekked west to escape the fighting and fearing resprisals from rival Tutsis.

Witnesses on a charter plane that flew over part of the road from the combat zone on Saturday, saw little sign of refugees, but church and other sources in Kisangani said that they suspected the refugees were hiding in the forest.
Foreign aid workers pulled out of eastern Zaire over a week ago as insecurity spread to the huge refugee camps of Goma and Bukavu. Refugees also fled from some of the camps.

The whereabouts of many of the 1.2 million Hutu refugees from those camps remains a mystery but reports filtering out of eastern Zaire talk of refugees dying from thirst and exhaustion. Aid groups fear epidemics of cholera and dysentery.
The Hutus fled Rwanda in 1994 fearing reprisals after Hutu hardliners massacred hundreds of thousands of Tutsis there. Zaire says Tutsi-led Rwanda is behind the revolt in the east.
The fighting in the east has also displaced several hundred thousand Zaireans plus Hutu refugees from Burundi.
